subject: Computer Networking
title: Internet Governance and Fragmentation
description: One-minute skill: Internet Governance and Fragmentation.

hook.text: The internet was born unified. Governments now split it into national intranets. A splinternet.

buildup.text: China's Firewall blocks Google and Facebook. Russia's RUNET can disconnect from the global net.

discovery.text: Data sovereignty laws keep data within borders. The EU, India, and Brazil each write own rules.

twist.text: Technical fragmentation follows political. Different DNS roots, CAs, and rules per country.

climax.text: ICANN and the IGF try to keep unity but can't enforce rules on sovereign nations.

punchline.text: The global internet is fragmenting. Unity faces political division.

quiz.question: What does internet fragmentation mean?
options: Countries creating separate, restricted versions of the internet
Physical cables being cut between countries

details.summary: Internet governance determines the rules, standards, and policies that shape how the global internet operates.
details.whyItMatters: Internet fragmentation threatens the global connectivity that drives innovation and commerce. Governance decisions made today will determine whether the internet remains open or splits into walled gardens.
takeaways: Organizations like ICANN, IETF, and ITU govern different internet aspects
Sovereign internet laws risk splitting the global network
Technical standards enable interoperability across all borders

faq.question: What is internet fragmentation?
faq.answer: Internet fragmentation occurs when governments create national firewalls, mandate local data storage, block foreign services, or develop alternative technical standards. China's Great Firewall and Russia's RuNet are examples.

faq.question: Who governs the internet?
faq.answer: No single entity controls the internet. ICANN manages domain names and IP allocation. IETF develops technical standards. Regional Internet Registries allocate IP addresses. The ITU coordinates spectrum. Governments set national policies.
